dxerr9.lib — Microsoft DirectX error-reporting library, as linked into lotrbfme.exe
===================================================================================

dxerr9.lib
  sha256  07f40f6799edceffb1d9532a5a42d1e8177bbf5a60f5e1b0c9975b9c2cfcb1b5
  size    3,710,046 bytes
  dated   2003-08-18
  from    DirectX 9.0 SDK Update (Summer 2003), Lib/DxErr9.lib

Why this exact SDK
------------------
The same archive that supplies it also supplies d3dx9.lib with sha256
9496d4ce606998c2ad7588f2db9aada3c59786515244482230fde0cd6099ed56 — byte for
byte the library already vendored at vendor/d3dx9/, which was pinned to this
release by the shader-assembler version stamped in the retail exe. One
extraction, both libraries: the provenance argument made for d3dx9 carries
over unchanged rather than being re-argued from scratch.

Region
------
RVA 0x00AD5401-0x00AFD502, immediately after the d3dx9 band ends at
0x00AD5000. The linker placed the two DirectX SDK static libraries adjacent,
which is what identified this one: a 163 KB contiguous run of unclaimed .text
comparing eax against 522 HRESULT constants (0x8876 Direct3D, 0x8878
DirectSound) and referencing the exe's E_ABORT / E_POINTER / D3DERR_
string tables.

Coverage
--------
The single member obj\i386\dxerr9.obj carries 14 .text sections totalling
164,226 bytes, one function each. All 14 place at distinct addresses and their
union covers 163,214 / 163,214 bytes of the band — 100.00%, with nothing left
over. Two of the fourteen (?StringCopyWorkerA, ?StringVPrintfWorkerA) are the
same helper also linked into d3dx9 and are already claimed there, so they are
not re-claimed here.

Rows sourced here carry `vendored=dxerr9-summer2003` and name the archive
member their bytes come from; ./build.sh extracts that member and byte-compares
it against retail like any other row.

Re-obtaining it
---------------
    https://archive.org/download/dx90updatesdk/dx90updatesdk.exe   (191 MB)

A WEXTRACT self-extractor wrapping a CAB wrapping the inner installer; `7z x`
handles every layer. Extract to a real filesystem, not a tmpfs scratch dir.

Licence
-------
Redistribution of the DirectX SDK libraries is governed by the DirectX SDK
EULA. The file is committed as a build input for byte-verification only: it is
read to prove that retail bytes match Microsoft's shipped code, and none of it
is compiled into or redistributed as part of any binary this repo produces.
